## Example 4.2 · A general argument {#ss4-example-4-2-ab .ar-lesson }

Consider an arithmetic series of $n$ terms with first term equal to $a$ and last term equal to $l$.

<div class="ar-subparts"><p><span>a)</span> Write down an expression for the sum of this series.</p><p><span>b)</span> By writing this expression in reverse order, deduce a formula for the sum of the first <span data-math="n">n</span> terms of an arithmetic series.</p></div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 20 · Example 4.2(a–b)</p>

::: notes

Students set up the two expressions in their booklet before the staged proof on the next slide. Use l as in the supplied question, then identify l=a_n later. The endpoint notation keeps the first formula independent of a separately known common difference.

:::
